meaning.observed: Direct evidence for the named operation in the stated profile and build. Guest playback or guest Maps navigation does not establish signed-in behavior.
meaning.partial: One or more relevant steps ran. The intended result or a necessary control remains unverified.
meaning.open: The records cited for the app do not demonstrate the named operation.

restart_persistence.evidence: The signed-in UI and account identifier survived client restart.

sign_in.evidence: With the delegated broker grant (eight scopes taken from YouTube's own code, 24-hour native consent) and the silent-token fix for the notification flag, the original app listed the account with its YouTube identity and signed in; the signed-in Subscriptions page showed the account avatar.

account_session.evidence: The account tab showed the account's own page, including its private Watch later and Liked videos lists.

video_playback.evidence: The original APK played a public clip to the end. Repeats included a retained guest profile. Signed-in playback and physical audibility remain open.

restart_persistence.evidence: After a full restart of the YouTube process, the app came back signed in: signed-in Subscriptions page and account avatar.

account_selection.evidence: On the fresh dedicated host (its own host and initially empty app data), Gmail's setup listed the test account and Take me to Gmail entered that account's mailbox. Westlake's per-app sync default is off, so Sync Gmail was turned on in Gmail's account settings; the first sync then filled the inbox.

mailbox_sync.evidence: In the earlier delegated configuration, original Gmail populated its inbox and opened an existing message after enabling sync and restarting.

refresh.evidence: After the network compat library fix, Gmail's automatic sync after start fetched the newly sent test message; it appeared in Primary and its body rendered. A manual pull with another new message was not repeated.

restart_persistence.evidence: The earlier configuration retained the account, inbox and automatic-sync preference across a client restart. The dedicated fresh-profile control stopped at setup. After the account provider was restored, it verified a newly restarted original Gmail process and the retained Primary inbox reappeared.

account_selection.evidence: Drive used the retained, consented account. The cited runs do not independently document an interactive account choice. Fresh dedicated Drive found no account and received authenticator unavailable when it asked to add one, including after connecting to both official services. With the dedicated Drive account connection restored, the provider returned one Android account and the official Play account content provider resolved. Drive still requested add-account and detached its window. The retained profile also failed on the current official-service configuration. Two dedicated cold starts captured 32 get_accounts replies from official Play services. All contained an empty typed account array. Drive requested add-account on each launch.

file_listing.evidence: My Drive listed the approved fixture after a process restart. The current account-path retest did not reach the file list.

file_open.evidence: The original Drive preview rendered the three expected lines of the 107-byte file. The current account-path retest did not reach the file list.

token_renewal.evidence: In one running Drive process, the last token was issued at 17:15:42 PST. Opening the fixture at 18:29:06, 73 minutes later and past the one-hour token lifetime, made Play services accept a silent request; the broker issued a new token under the native consent, and the fixture content rendered.

restart_persistence.evidence: The same profile listed and opened the fixture after restart. Its contents could have been cached. The current account-path retest did not reach the file list.

startup.evidence: Original Maps opened in guest mode.

map_tiles.evidence: The guest UI displayed labeled map tiles.

search.evidence: Guest place search returned a result with the services connected. Signed-in place search remains open.

real_location.evidence: OpenHarmony accepted two requests during the temporary permission grant. No real fix was delivered. Permission was restored to Deny. With GNSS disabled, the adapter now reports GPS disabled to Android and withholds explicit GPS requests. Original Maps exercised the change on its dedicated host. Network provider configuration and a physical fix remain open. A board fixture verified provider selection, source filtering and per-provider caches on the rebuilt adapter. Original Maps queried last location with its host permission denied. It received zero physical fixes.

route_preview.evidence: The guest directions screen displayed a route preview between specified endpoints.

restart_persistence.evidence: The retained guest configuration survived restart and repeated the directions flow.

sign_in.evidence: On the earlier shared host, Google accepted basic profile and email consent in web sign-in, then Uber displayed “Sorry, we could not find that page”. On the current dedicated host the signed rider app displayed its welcome page. The trip-link window disappeared before a Google tap, and the normal launch displayed the Uber logo before the board returned to Gmail. Rider sign-in remains partial.

account_session.gap: No authenticated rider session was observed.

destination_search.gap: Uber opened onboarding for a link with fixed endpoints. The user did not exercise in-app destination search.

sign_in.evidence: Spotify showed the Facebook form and the full main-document origin in its own WebView on the dedicated host. Submission and authenticated return remain open. With the standalone Facebook app already running under another UID, Spotify still displayed the empty form in its own window. The native provider lookup missed twice more before the form appeared. The original APK declares a browser callback and the installed OpenHarmony host advertises only its home ability.
